problem_statement: This is the nuxt-shadcn-dashboard admin app (the dianprata Nuxt dashboard template): a Shadcn-Vue dashboard whose Home (overview), Tasks and Kanban pages all render inside one shared shell layout with a left sidebar (Acme Inc team switcher, General / Apps / Pages navigation) and a sticky top header with breadcrumbs. The pages read their sample data and avatars from the local /avatars and /public assets. The team wants a small, consistent 'Data coverage' rail pinned to the top of the content area on the main dashboard pages that summarises how much of the connected dataset has synced — a labelled row of four metric tiles (records synced, sources connected, coverage window, last refresh) plus a coverage-window toggle (7 days / 30 days / 90 days) whose readout names the window that is currently selected. Ship the Data coverage rail so it (1) appears at the top of the content on the shared dashboard pages — Home, Tasks AND Kanban, not just the Home page, (2) lays out its tile row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the dashboard's own light Shadcn card styling (card surface, hairline border, foreground text — not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps its coverage-window readout in sync so that after a user selects the 90-day window the readout re-reads and names the live selection. Keep the rest of the app — the sidebar, the header, the page content, the local avatar assets — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Data coverage' rail at the top of the content area on the main dashboard pages — Home, Tasks AND Kanban — with identical rail markup, not only the Home page.
The rail shows a 'Data coverage' heading and a row of four metric tiles (Records synced, Sources connected, Coverage window, Last refresh).
The tile row must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in the dashboard's own light Shadcn language (card surface, hairline border, foreground/muted text), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the coverage-window toggle (7 days / 30 days / 90 days): after selecting the 90-day window the readout (id coverage-readout) must read 'Coverage window: 90 days' — it must re-read the live selection, not rewrite a stale captured value.
Preserve the sidebar, the header, the page content and the local avatar assets with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the dianprata nuxt-shadcn-dashboard template, a runnable Nuxt Shadcn-Vue admin dashboard whose Home, Tasks and Kanban pages share one sidebar-plus-header shell layout and whose avatars and social art are served from the local /avatars and /public folders. The Data coverage rail is a shared Vue component rendered by the shared dashboard layout at the top of the content on the main pages (Home, Tasks, Kanban); its four metric tiles summarise dataset sync coverage, grounding the rail in the app's own dashboard story. The coverage-window toggle drives a small live readout in the same component. The remote NuxtHub deploy module and the remote font providers were neutralised so the dashboard builds statically and runs offline with no network fetches. The responsive tile row, the light Shadcn design integration and the coverage-window readout wiring were designed by hand for this dashboard, not bulk-generated.
design_constraints: Implement the Data coverage rail as one shared component reused across the dashboard pages so a single source of truth reaches Home, Tasks and Kanban; do not paste divergent copies or build a detached widget.
The tile row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the tile spacing must stay legible.
The rail must adopt the dashboard's own Shadcn card surface / hairline border / foreground text tokens and typography so it reads as part of the dashboard, not a foreign dark block.
The coverage-window readout must reflect the CURRENTLY selected window after every toggle click by reading the live selection, so it can never go stale relative to what the user selected.
Do not remove or regress the sidebar, the header, the page content or the local avatar assets.

change_completion: The Data coverage rail is present at the top of the content on Home, Tasks AND Kanban (the shared rail reaches all main dashboard pages, not just Home).
After selecting the 90-day window on the Home page, the coverage readout (coverage-readout) updates to 'Coverage window: 90 days' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from '30 days'.
design_consistency: The rail on the in-viewport states matches the reference's light Shadcn card styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The rail adopts the dashboard's own card surface, hairline border and foreground text tokens so it reads as part of the dashboard across the pages.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tile row wraps.
mobile_initial, mobile_rail_home and tablet_rail_home keep the Data coverage rail readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The sidebar, the header and the page content remain present and functional across the pages.
The local avatar assets and the dashboard pages are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the dashboard home and responsive shell.
desktop_tasks and desktop_kanban protect the existing Tasks and Kanban pages and carry the Data coverage rail.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home show the Data coverage rail on the home page and must render the light card rail without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_tasks and desktop_rail_kanban protect the rail's presence on the Tasks and Kanban pages.
tablet_rail_home protects the rail's tablet layout without overflow.
desktop_window_toggle selects the 90-day coverage window; the readout must then read 'Coverage window: 90 days'.
